evidence: Full CDIAL haḍḍa explicitly gives Punjabi/Hindi haḍḍī, Gujarati/Marathi hāḍ and, in the addendum, Kotgarhi hàṛkɔ, Jaunsari hāḍkī and Garhwali hāḍgu with a hāḍku comparison. The selected simple and k-extended bone forms fit this documented family; vowels, voicing, retroflexion, optional h, nasalization and inflection remain as elicited. The medial k extension is directly attested, not reconstructed from the survey alone. Turner calls the connection with asthi/aṣṭhi very doubtful; no such deeper ancestry is asserted. Regional IA transmission remains unresolved.

Full CDIAL haḍḍa explicitly gives Phalura haḍḍuṅg bone. Phal survey haḍūŋk fits this exact regional extended form with source vowel length, nasal notation and final k/g voicing retained. Regional transmission and the internal history of the extension remain qualified; the entire response is linked rather than treating ūŋk as an independently established component.

Full CDIAL haḍḍa explicitly gives Kashmiri aḍa bones, eastern Assamese hār/Bengali hāṛ/Oriya hāṛa and feminine haḍḍī bone in Hindi/Punjabi. The selected eastern aṛa/ar and Adivasi Oriya āḍi/āṛi/aṛi/haṛi/aḍi bone forms are grouped with this regional family, with h loss, rhotic versus stop spelling and final vowels preserved. This does not assert a Kashmiri loan to eastern languages. Regional history remains qualified, and the doubtful asthi comparison is not adopted.
